question: A project lead has a single sentence from a director: "We need faster case handling." She wants to use Claude to turn this into a requirement set that goes to stakeholders for sign-off with no open questions left once it is drafted. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) List the open gaps; draft the requirement set; state the outcome and who is affected; take the gaps to stakeholders.
B) State the outcome and who is affected; list the open gaps; take the gaps to stakeholders; draft the requirement set.
C) Take the gaps to stakeholders; list the open gaps; draft the requirement set; state the outcome and who is affected.
D) Draft the requirement set; state the outcome and who is affected; list the open gaps; take the gaps to stakeholders.
correct_answers: B) State the outcome and who is affected; list the open gaps; take the gaps to stakeholders; draft the requirement set.
explanations: Incorrect. This option drafts the requirement set in step two, before the outcome is even stated in step three and before the gaps are ever taken to stakeholders in step four -- the draft goes out carrying the same open questions the project lead wanted resolved first, and the closing stakeholder step happens too late to change a draft that already exists.

Correct. Naming the outcome and who is affected turns the director's one sentence into a target the gaps can be measured against; listing what is still unknown surfaces the open questions; taking those to stakeholders closes them before anything is written down; only then does the draft go out with no open questions left, which is exactly what the project lead needs.

Incorrect. This option takes gaps to stakeholders in step one, before any gap has been listed in step two, so there is nothing yet to ask stakeholders about; it also drafts the requirement set before the outcome and audience are named, so the draft is written without knowing what it is meant to achieve or for whom.

Incorrect. The project lead wants a requirement set with no open questions left once it is drafted, so drafting cannot be the first step: nothing is known yet about the outcome, who is affected, or what is missing when this option's draft is written, and that draft is never revisited after the outcome is stated or the gaps are surfaced.
